items.stem: Before designing training, a needs analysis most importantly determines whether:

options.text: The budget is large enough for a two-day course
options.rationale: Budget sizing follows the decision to train, not the needs analysis itself.

options.text: The performance gap is actually caused by a lack of skill or knowledge
options.rationale: Correct: training only helps when the cause is a skill or knowledge gap.
Vendor availability does not establish the need.
Popularity is not a basis for a training need.

items.explanation: Correct: training only helps when the cause is a skill or knowledge gap.

items.stem: Which TWO are signs a program is being evaluated beyond simple satisfaction? (Select TWO)

options.text: It measures whether learners can demonstrate the new skill
options.rationale: Correct: a learning-level measure goes beyond reaction scores.

options.text: It tracks whether behaviour changed back on the job
options.rationale: Correct: behaviour change is a higher evaluation level than reaction.

options.text: It counts how many people attended
options.rationale: Attendance is an input, not an evaluation of effect.

options.text: It records the average happy-sheet rating only
options.rationale: Satisfaction alone is the lowest evaluation level.

items.explanation: Correct: a learning-level measure goes beyond reaction scores.; Correct: behaviour change is a higher evaluation level than reaction.
